### packages, data cleanup, and summaries

```{r packages, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r data-cleanup, echo = FALSE}
# data import and cleanup ----
flu_data <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cdcepi/FluSight-forecast-hub/refs/heads/main/target-data/target-hospital-admissions.csv")
flu_data_orig <- flu_data # original copy of data

## function to assign season given date
## seasons defined as epiweek 40 to epiweek 39 (roughly October to October)
find_season <- function(date) {
  date <- as.Date(date)
  epiyr <- epiyear(date)
  epiwk <- epiweek(date)
  start_yr <- ifelse(epiwk >= 40, epiyr, epiyr - 1)
  end_yr <- start_yr + 1
  paste0(start_yr,"-",end_yr)
}

flu_data <- flu_data |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date), week = epiweek(date), year = epiyear(date), season = as.factor(find_season(date))) # adding columns for epiweek/epiyear

# flu_data$season <- find_season(flu_data$date) # adding column for season
# flu_data$season <- as.factor(flu_data$season)

summary(flu_data$season)
head(flu_data)
```

### choropleth maps (updated 10-30-26)
```{r choropleths-1, include = FALSE}
flu_maxes <- flu_data |>
  group_by(location_name, season) |>
  slice_max(weekly_rate) |>
  relocate(location_name, location, season, date, weekly_rate, value)

states_48 <- states(cb = TRUE) |>
  filter(!STUSPS %in% c("AK", "HI", "PR", "GU", "VI", "AS", "MP"))

seasons <- unique(flu_data$season)
```


```{r choropleths-2, echo = FALSE}
peak_flu_choropleth <- function (given_season) {
  date_lims = c(as.Date(paste0(substr(given_season, 1, 4), "-10-01")),
              as.Date(paste0(substr(given_season, 6, 9), "-03-31")))
   
  flu_maxes_filtered <- flu_maxes |>
    filter(location_name != "US", season == given_season) |>
    rename(GEOID = location)
  
  flu_maxes_sf <- left_join(states_48, flu_maxes_filtered, by = "GEOID")
  
  choropleth_map <- ggplot(flu_maxes_sf, aes(fill = date)) +
    geom_sf() +
    coord_sf(datum = NA, xlim = c(-125, -66), ylim = c(24, 50), expand = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "date", # date transformation on date column
                         limits = date_lims,
                         labels = scales::label_date("%B %d"), # Month day format
                         option = "viridis", 
                         guide = guide_colorbar(barheight = unit(6, "cm"), reverse = TRUE),
                         # extends colorbar to prevent overlapping, puts older at top
                         breaks = seq(from = date_lims[1], 
                                      to = date_lims[2], 
                                      by = 14)) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(title = paste("Peak Weekly Influenza Hospitalization Rate in", given_season), fill = "Date")
  
  return(choropleth_map)
}

choropleth_maps <- sapply(seasons[1:5], peak_flu_choropleth)
choropleth_maps
```

### finding peaks by state/season (updated 10-30-26)

While I just used `findpeaks(threshold = 1)` to try to identify peaks, I tried smoothing out the data using a LOESS regression model, setting the $\alpha = 0.3$.

```{r loess}
flu_loess <- flu_data |>
  group_by(location_name, season) |>
  arrange(date) |>
  mutate(time_index = row_number(),
         loess_smoothed = predict(loess(weekly_rate ~ time_index, 
                                        span = 0.4, 
                                        na.action = na.exclude))) |>
  ungroup()

get_peaks <- function(group_data, season_input) {
  initial_peaks <- findpeaks(group_data, minpeakdistance = 4, threshold = 1)
  peaks <- if (is.null(initial_peaks)) {matrix(data = NA_real_, ncol = 4)} else {initial_peaks}
  
  dates_in_order <- flu_data |>
    filter(season == season_input) |>
    select(date) |> unique() |> as.matrix() |> sort()
  
  peaks[,2] <- dates_in_order[peaks[,2]]
  peaks[,3] <- dates_in_order[peaks[,3]]
  peaks[,4] <- dates_in_order[peaks[,4]]
  
  return(peaks)
}

state_peaks <- flu_loess|>
  filter(!season %in% c("2021-2022", "2026-2027")) |>
  group_by(location_name, season) |>
  reframe(loess_peak = get_peaks(loess_smoothed, season)[,1],
          peak_date = get_peaks(loess_smoothed, season)[,2])

peak_plot <- function (given_state, given_season) {
  flu_loess_filtered <- flu_loess |> filter(location_name == given_state, season == given_season)
  
  plot <- ggplot(data = flu_loess_filtered, 
  mapping = aes(x = as.Date(date), y = weekly_rate)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.5) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.4) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Date", y = "Weekly Rate", title = paste0("Weekly Hospitalization Rates in ", given_state, ", ", given_season))
  return(plot)
}

lapply(seasons[2:5], peak_plot, given_state = "Virginia")
lapply(seasons[2:5], peak_plot, given_state = "Wyoming")
```
